# Vector integrals

Line, area, and volume measures and their orientations are defined in
[calculus, fluxes, and conservation](operators.qmd#integration-jacobians-and-integral-theorems).
That treatment owns the divergence and Stokes identities used below.

For a worked circulation check, take solid-body planar rotation
$\mathbf u=(-\Omega y,\Omega x,0)$ around a counterclockwise circle of radius $a$.
The tangential speed is $\Omega a$, so $\oint\mathbf u\cdot d\mathbf l=2\pi\Omega a^2$.
Its vorticity is $2\Omega\mathbf e_z$; integrating through the disk gives the same
$2\Omega\pi a^2$. The orientation fixes the sign. This example uses Stokes'
theorem @ArfkenWeber2005, Section 1.12.
